UNDERSTANDING CURRENT ELECTRICITY
====

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN
----
• Say what understanding current electricity means in plain words.
• Give one clear example linked to Current Electricity.
• Correct one common mistake about this page.

INTRODUCTION
----
Understanding Current Electricity. Get clear on current electricity before moving on. How would you explain current electricity to a classmate in one minute? Use this anchor: Distinguish between potential difference and electromotive force as used in electricity,. Clue from the topic: Current, voltage and resistance. Check every example on this page against that anchor.

MAIN NOTES
----
• Electric current is the rate of flow of charge; potential difference (voltage) drives that flow.
• Ohm’s law (ohmic conductors): V = IR.
• Power: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
• Series: same current through each component; parallel: same voltage across branches.
• Use correct units: V in volts, I in amperes, R in ohms, P in watts.

WORKED EXAMPLE
----
Worked example — Ohm’s law:
A conductor has resistance 6 Ω and potential difference 8 V. Find the current.

Working:

2. Substitute values: I = 8 / 6
3. I = 1.333
Final Answer: 1.333 A
